newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on European buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on European buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended stronger on Friday from New York's previous close on healthy afternoon buying from Europe, gold dealers said.
"We saw some (European) short-covering and buying on strength in the white metals," said one dealer at an international bank.
Bullion ended at US$355.00/50 an ounce on Friday against New York's US$354.10/60 close on Thursday.
Morning trade drifted quietly and volumes were slim as not many dealers showed interest in selling around $354.30 per ounce, gold traders said.
Gold had found temporary support at around $352 per ounce, they said.
When Europe entered the market after noon, prices firmed on brisk buying, dealers said.
Gold could test $357 per ounce, if Friday's small afternoon rebound was not swatted back by heavy fund selling, they said.
Local gold ended HK$8 higher at HK$3,281 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -5.00 from its previous fix at +1.00
